To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the critical behavior of scale-free networks is determined by a single exponent gamma'=(gamma - mu)/(1-mu).

the critical behavior of scale-free networks with interactions is determined by the degree-dependent interaction strength, which can absorb the effect from the degree distribution, and that the critical behavior is universal in the sense that it is independent of the topology.

the critical behavior of scale-free networks can be controlled by tuning the interactions, and that a simple mapping between the interaction parameter and the exponent of the degree distribution allows the universality classes to be tuned continuously.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the effect of degree-degree correlations on the structure of scale-free networks.
the interplay of interactions and topology in complex networks.
how the critical behavior of scale-free systems is affected by the topology of the network and by the interactions between the nodes.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the critical properties of a system with degree-dependent interactions are identical to those of a system with topology-dependent interactions, and that the critical behavior of the system is independent of the type of interactions.
the topology of a network determines its critical behavior, but the interaction can modify the universality class.
the topology and interaction of scale-free networks are equivalent in their effect on the critical behavior.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
topology and interactions can be traded with each other.
the critical behavior of scale-free networks is not only determined by their topology, but also by the degree-dependent interactions.

, in a scale-free network with topology-dependent interactions, a shift of the exponent gamma of the power-law degree distribution P(q), which is conventionally considered as a topology parameter, is equivalent to a shift of the interaction parameter mu, which is conventionally used to describe the degree dependence of interactions.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the topology of a network can be replaced by a set of effective interactions, and vice versa.
, for scale-free networks, interactions can substitute topology as the tuning parameter of critical phenomena.
the critical behavior of a scale-free network can be tuned not only by changing the network topology but also by modifying the interactions.
